name: agy

detect.detect_notes: `agy --version` prints a bare semver ("1.2.0", live 2026-09-10). On this machine agy is a single native agy.exe directly on PATH (no npm shim, no script wrapper), so detect.npm_exe/npm_entry do not apply: the PATH scan resolves the .exe and spawns it without a shell. The binary self-updates in place (an in-place 1.1.27 -> 1.1.28 update was observed in the 2026-09-09 probe report; this record is calibrated on 1.2.0); version drift policy applies — re-run probes after upgrades. [2026-10-27 re-check on 1.4.8: still a bare semver; still a single native exe, but an official-installer reinstall moved it from a machine-local custom directory to the official default target directory, which the installer also adds to User PATH (the old directory and its PATH entry were removed). bin:"agy" survived the move because detection is PATH-based; only absolute overrides such as a paidan config endpoints.overrides.agy.bin needed repointing.]

command.mode_args_notes: AGY exposes --dangerously-skip-permissions (introduced 1.3.5, native --help 2026-10-15; re-verified on 1.4.8 with native --help 2026-10-27, which also lists --mode accept-edits|auto|plan and --effort low|medium|high|xhigh|max — paidan still sends no --effort). unattended uses --mode accept-edits plus that explicit auto-approval flag; read-only and workspace-write retain plan/accept-edits without it. No native settings are rewritten, no sandbox flag is added. The skip flag is passed on fresh and resumed invocations. Older manifest evidence about native allow rules describes restricted modes, not the new unattended path. Real account/permission smoke status is recorded separately.
command.argv_notes: Prompt rides argv (-p <prompt>) like the suite adapter (prompt_transport=argv); there is no single-shot stdin text mode (--input-format stream-json is a multi-turn NDJSON protocol, out of v0 scope). Windows command-line budget applies to the prompt bytes (suite cap 26 KiB). --print-timeout is always passed: native default is 5m, window 30s..120m; 30m preserves the historical operational envelope. 1.2.0 timeout semantics: partial output + exit 0 + status SUCCESS + stderr marker, surfaced as the print-timeout-partial-output refusal signal. Native config (~/.gemini) decides auth and default model; paidan never stages or overrides beyond the flags above. [2026-09-18 1.2.5: P1-write=pass, P2-readonly-refusal=indeterminate, P3-resume=pass. Native settings unchanged. Isolated paidan homes used; model/effort followed the user-selected combination.]

env._env_notes: AGY_CLI_DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE=true is pinned (same as the suite): without it, headless runs still touched the native updater (update_status.json flipped to 'Update failed, please install from website', last_check.timestamp refreshed; live 2026-09-10) even though antigravity-cli/settings.json carries update.mode=none; with the env var, updater files stay untouched (verified). HOME/USERPROFILE are NOT set: agy runs against the user's real ~/.gemini (zero-copy native home; Google OAuth lives in the OS keyring, unaffected by HOME isolation). Paidan never stages or copies agy config/credentials.

fs.read.via: view_file requires a native read_file allow rule (request-review default auto-denies it headless, verified 2026-09-10); on Windows 1.2.0 only the unscoped form read_file(*) matched — every scoped path form tested (drive-stripped dir, dir/*, full-drive, backslash) failed to authorize view_file, an upstream limitation to revisit on upgrades. grep_search/list_dir work unlisted. Production native settings carry read_file(*).

fs.write.via: RECALIBRATED 2026-09-10 on agy 1.2.0 (supersedes the 1.1.28 scoped-rule story AND the same-day intermediate 'unscoped-only' note, which was mechanism-confounded): write_to_file is artifact-confined upstream — a non-artifact target dies at permission conversion ('not a valid artifact path; artifacts must be in brain/<conversation>/', invalid_args) BEFORE any write_file rule is evaluated, so write_file allow rules are irrelevant to deliverable writes. Deliverables actually ride run_command (shell), gated by command(*); and run_command starts in agy's own scratch dir (~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch, pwd-verified), NOT the run cwd — models must be told absolute paths (paidan injects a cwd hint into the task text, command.prompt_cwd_hint). SOFT because deliverable writes are shell-ridden and not path-governed; reliability depends on the model using absolute paths. read-only (--mode plan) produced no writes (P2 pass on 1.2.0). Evidence: 4-variant rule matrix + 3 raw-stream direct runs + brain transcript of run_20260910_ca92a967.

shell.exec.via: run_command auto-approved headless when the native allow rule command(*) is present (verified 2026-09-10: output captured, DONE, no denial); without the rule it auto-denies (request-review + no prompt channel). SOFT because shell is NOT path-confined without --sandbox: on 2026-09-10 a workspace-write run's shell leg wrote a duplicate deliverable into the paidan CALLER's cwd (outside the run cwd; run_command starts from an inherited PWD-ish directory on Windows — the suite documented this as 'run_command may start from C:\'); write_file tool writes stay natively path-governed, shell writes are not. Under --sandbox run_command demands an unsandboxed grant headless runs can never receive — paidan does not pass --sandbox. 1.2.0 addendum: run_command starts in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/scratch regardless of the spawn cwd (pwd-verified 2026-09-10); 'context canceled' tool errors observed at turn end on otherwise-successful runs are upstream shell-leg teardown noise (1.1.28 and 1.2.0 alike).

net.fetch.via: read_url_content tool exists and the native allow rule read_url(*) is in place, but no live fetch probe was run in the 2026-09-10 native matrix; 1.1.28 changed URL fetching to default-Ask (probe report 2026-09-09 §8), so expect auto-deny without the rule

interact.ask.via: headless has no approval channel: every ask/unlisted action is auto-denied and lands in result.denied_actions with the stderr jetski line (verified repeatedly 2026-09-10); ask write_file(*) is exactly this backstop

permission.presets_notes: read-only=--mode plan (soft/unverified enforcement); workspace-write=--mode accept-edits (native rules); unattended=--mode accept-edits --dangerously-skip-permissions (native 1.3.5 highest headless approval flag). The skip flag does not claim OS isolation or remove the native artifact/cwd limitations. fs.write/shell.exec remain soft until live evidence supports stronger claims.

denial_evidence.via: three in-band channels, all live-verified 2026-09-10: (1) result.denied_actions[] e.g. {action:write_file,display_name:WriteToFile} for ask/plan auto-denies; (2) step_update state=ERROR tool_info.error TOOL_ERROR messages ('permission check failed ... Matches user-configured deny rule', 'user denied permission ...') for explicit rules; (3) stderr 'jetski: no output produced — a tool required the "<action>" permission ... auto-denied'. Empty response with SUCCESS is a legal terminal shape and stays evidence, not automatic failure

permission.headless_notes: unattended explicitly auto-approves tool permission requests using --dangerously-skip-permissions. Restricted modes retain native allow/deny rules. No interactive approval bridge or native configuration writes.

resume.notes: Session handle = conversation_id (UUID) from the init/result events. Cross-process resume via --conversation <id> verified 2026-09-10 (1.2.0): recalled prior content exactly, and resolution is machine-wide — the same id resumed from a DIFFERENT cwd too (supersedes the 2026-09-09 probe report's cwd-scoped assumption for explicit ids). --continue/-c picks the most recent conversation of the current cwd (verified). mode_args are re-spliced on resume (no resume_argv): --mode and --conversation coexist in one argv (suite adapter shape; a resumed run re-tiers from the new invocation). Concurrent resume of the same conversation was not probed; treat as forbidden (transcript interleaving, claude-analog).

models.notes: Native agy models catalog. Authentication/account cannot be inferred from model IDs; connection remains unknown unless native config states it. Model IDs may encode tiers. Newer native --effort/model combinations are not yet supported by this adapter; follow native effort. Fixed selections bind to the current native metadata context; changed/unbound defaults require user choice. Current catalog membership is checked before fixed dispatch; credentials/quota remain unverified.

native_preflight.notes: Read-only check of the user-maintained native permission rules (2026-09-10/11 calibration). read_file(*) gates view_file (fs.read); command(*) gates run_command — which is what deliverable writes actually ride on agy 1.2.0 (write_to_file is confined to brain/<conversation>/ artifacts, so a write_file allow rule is irrelevant to deliverables and is deliberately NOT required; requiring it would push users to widen permissions for no effect — codex P1-12). Missing rules surface as a submit warning and a doctor status; paidan never writes this file (invariant 4).

parser_notes: stdout NDJSON: init (conversation_id, cwd, permission_mode) -> step_update (agent_response text_delta accumulation; tool ERROR events carry permission TOOL_ERRORs) -> exactly one terminal result (status, response, conversation_id cross-checked against init, usage input/output/cache_read tokens, denied_actions). finalText = result.response, falling back to accumulated agent_response deltas with a warning when no result event arrives. Non-JSON lines, mid-line EOF and conflicting conversation ids degrade the parser. detectRefusals reads the stderr jetski auto-deny line and the print-timeout marker (partial output + exit 0 + SUCCESS; 1.2.0 timeout semantics). Evidence: live captures 2026-09-10 (1.1.x era probe set agy-native; raw scratch deleted 2026-09-13, verdicts distilled here) plus the same-day 1.2.0 recalibration runs, and the retired external-agent-suite agy adapter (archived 2026-09-12).

capabilities._capabilities_notes: No native background for -p runs. Cancel = paidan taskkill tree (v0). Upstream >= 1.1.20 made exit codes semantic (non-zero = cascade failure); print-timeout and soft denials still exit 0 — terminal judgment is evidence-first, never exit-code-only.
